facts.statement: Kryptops is an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Niger.
facts.quote: Kryptops (meaning "covered face") is an extinct genus of possibly chimeric abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Niger.

facts.statement: Fossils were collected in 2000 by a University of Chicago expedition led by Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: The fossils were collected in 2000 by a University of Chicago expedition to Niger led by American paleontologist Paul Sereno.

facts.statement: The genus and species were described in 2008 by Paul Sereno and Steve Brusatte.
facts.quote: They were then described in 2008 by Sereno and Steve Brusatte.

facts.statement: The genus contains a single species named Kryptops palaios.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Kryptops palaios.

facts.statement: Kryptops is estimated to have been between 6 and 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: Its length is estimated to be around 6 - 7 m, making it smaller than later genera such as Carnotaurus.

facts.statement: Kryptops was a large carnivorous dinosaur with robust upper jaws and highly serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, Kryptops is a large, carnivorous dinosaur with highly serrated teeth (bearing many denticles) and robust upper jaws.

facts.statement: The outer surface of the maxilla features grooves and rugosities that suggest it was covered in a keratinous structure.
facts.quote: The outer surface of its maxilla features deep striations, grooves, and rugosities, indicating it was covered in a tightly adhering integumentary structure like keratin.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Aptian and Albian ages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: These layers belong to the Elrhaz Formation, which dates to the Aptian and Albian ages of the Early Cretaceous, around 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: A maxilla was collected 15 meters away from a set of postcranial elements including vertebrae, ribs, the sacrum, and the pelvis.
facts.quote: During the expedition, a maxilla (main tooth-bearing bone of the upper jaw) of a theropod was collected 15 m away from a set of postcranial elements consisting of three dorsal (back) vertebrae, two ribs, the sacrum, and the pelvis.

facts.statement: The fossils were designated as the holotype specimen for the new genus and species Kryptops palaios.
facts.quote: Sereno and Steve Brusatte described the fossils as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of a new genus and species of abelisaurid in 2008, named Kryptops palaios.

facts.statement: The generic name Kryptops means "covered face" in Ancient Greek, referencing the unique anatomy of the maxilla.
facts.quote: The generic name derives from the Ancient Greek words krypto, meaning covered, and ops, meaning face, referencing the unique anatomy of the maxilla.

facts.statement: The holotype individual is an adult estimated to be about 6 to 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype individual is large for an abelisaurid, belonging to an adult about 6 - 7 m in length.

facts.statement: The preserved maxilla has a tooth row length of 15 centimeters but is missing its tip and some tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The maxilla has a preserved tooth row length of 15 cm and is missing its tip, some of the alveolar margin (the upper edge of the maxilla that supports the tooth sockets), and the tooth crowns.

facts.statement: The left maxilla preserves 11 tooth positions but likely held 17 or 18 when complete.
facts.quote: The left maxilla preserves 11 alveoli (tooth positions) but likely bore 17 or 18 alveoli when complete, based on the related genus Rugops.

facts.statement: The rough texture may imply a keratinous covering on the maxillae rather than scales, though Carnotaurus skulls were scaly.
facts.quote: This may imply a keratinous integument on the maxillae instead of scales, giving the genus its name, though the skull of Carnotaurus was scaly.

facts.statement: The scalloped margins of the posterior ramus are identified as the only valid unique feature of Kryptops.
facts.quote: Delcourt identified this is as the only valid autapomorphy of Kryptops.

facts.statement: The tooth crowns are relatively flat and wide with about 15 serrations for every 5 millimeters.
facts.quote: Their crowns are relatively flat and wide, as in other abelisaurids, and have about 15 serrations for every 5 mm.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers suggested Kryptops palaios might be a chimera where postcranial remains belong to a carcharodontosaurid like Eocarcharia.
facts.quote: In 2012, Matthew Carrano and colleagues considered Kryptops palaios to be a chimera (specimen composed of multiple species), and stated that its postcranial remains, especially the pelvis and sacrum, may actually belong to a carcharodontosaurid, possibly Eocarcharia.

facts.statement: In 2018, Rafael Delcourt questioned the validity of Kryptops, suggesting it may be a nomen dubium due to having only one unique feature.
facts.quote: In 2018, paleontologist Rafael Delcourt questioned the validity of Kryptops, suggesting that, due to the presence of only one autapomorphy (unique feature) of the maxilla, Kryptops may be a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that metriacanthosaurids radiated globally during the Early Cretaceous based on the simultaneous presence of related fossils in Europe, Africa, and Asia.
facts.quote: Based on these results, they further suggested that metriacanthosaurids radiated across the world during the Early Cretaceous, as demonstrated by the roughly simultaneous presence of Erectopus in Europe, the "Kryptops" postcrania in Africa, and Siamotyrannus in Asia.

facts.statement: Kryptops belongs to the family Abelisauridae, a group of theropod dinosaurs that lived from the Jurassic through the Cretaceous until the mass extinction event.
facts.quote: Abelisauridae is a group of theropod dinosaurs that existed during the Cretaceous (and potentially earlier in the Jurassic) up until the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

facts.statement: Kryptops is considered one of the oldest-known abelisaurids, which is critical for understanding the evolution of the family.
facts.quote: Kryptops and Rugops are some of the oldest-known abelisaurids, making them critical to understanding the evolution and diversification of Abelisauridae.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the maxilla of Kryptops displays a mix of traits found in both early and late Cretaceous abelisaurids.
facts.quote: Sereno and Brusatte noted that Kryptops' maxilla bore a mix of characteristics seen in other basal abelisaurids as well as derived members from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: In a 2008 analysis, Sereno and Brusatte classified Kryptops as the earliest diverging abelisaurid, placing it before Rugops and Rajasaurus but before Majungasaurus and Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2008 phylogenetic analysis, Sereno and Brusatte recovered Kryptops as the earliest diverging abelisaurid, followed by Rugops and Rajasaurus, more basal than Majungasaurus and Carnotaurus.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses from 2024 and 2025 suggest Kryptops is a more derived taxon, diverging after Rugops and closer to brachyrostrans and majungasaurines than previously thought.
facts.quote: Multiple phylogenetic analyses from 2024 and 2025 recovered Kryptops as a more derived taxon, more closely related to the brachyrostrans and majungasaurines than in previous work, and diverging after Rugops.

facts.statement: The genus Kryptops was named by Sereno and Brusatte in 2008.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sereno & Brusatte, 2008

facts.statement: The species K. palaios was named by Sereno and Brusatte in 2008.
facts.quote: species_authority: Sereno & Brusatte, 2008

facts.statement: Kryptops was described by Paul Sereno and Stephen Brusatte in 2008, with only one species known: K. palaios.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio fue descrito por Paul Sereno y Stephen Brusatte en el 2008, con una sola especie hasta la fecha: K. palaios.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MNN GAD1 includes a maxilla with teeth, vertebrae, ribs, and the pelvic girdle and sacrum, belonging to an adult approximately 6 to 7 meters long.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MNN GAD1, incluye un maxilar con algunos dientes, vértebras, costillas, y la cintura pélvica y sacro, perteneciendo a un adulto cerca de 6 a 7 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The specimen shows a highly marked maxilla with pits and blood vessel impressions, suggesting a firm attachment of a facial covering, possibly made of keratin.
facts.quote: Este espécimen representa uno de los abelisáuridos conocidos más antiguos, presentando la cara maxilar muy marcada con la presencia de hoyos y de impresiones de vasos sanguíneos indicando que había una cubierta unida firmemente a la cara, quizás de queratina.

facts.statement: Carrano and colleagues argued that Kryptops palaios is a chimera, suggesting its postcranial remains found 15 meters from the holotype maxilla actually belong to a carcharodontosaurid, possibly Eocarcharia dinops.
facts.quote: Carrano et al., por otra parte, consideraron a Kryptops palaios como una quimera, y afirmaron que sus restos postcraneales, especialmente la pelvis y el sacro, hallados a unos 15 metros del maxilar holotipo, en realidad pertenecen a un carcarodontosáurido, posiblemente a Eocarcharia dinops.

facts.statement: Kryptops shared its environment with theropods including the carcharodontosaurid Eocarcharia, the spinosaurid Suchomimus, and the noasaurid Afromimus.
facts.quote: Kryptops lived alongside several other dinosaurs. These included other theropods, such as Eocarcharia (known from a chimeric combination of carcharodontosaurid and propobable spinosaurid material), the spinosaurid Suchomimus, and the putative noasaurid Afromimus.

facts.statement: The habitat of Kryptops included megaherbivores such as the hadrosauriforms Ouranosaurus and Lurdusaurus, the dryosaurid Elrhazosaurus, and the sauropods Nigersaurus and an unnamed titanosaur.
facts.quote: Several megaherbivores like the hadrosauriforms Ouranosaurus and Lurdusaurus, dryosaurid Elrhazosaurus, and two sauropods, the rebbachisaurid Nigersaurus and an unnamed titanosaur, have been unearthed from Gadoufaoua.

facts.statement: Kryptops likely inhabited habitats dominated by inland floodplains or riparian zones.
facts.quote: It likely lived in habitats dominated by inland floodplains (a riparian zone).

facts.statement: The aquatic fauna found in Kryptops' habitat consisted entirely of freshwater inhabitants.
facts.quote: The aquatic fauna consists entirely of freshwater inhabitants.

facts.statement: Kryptops lived in what is now Africa during the late Cretaceous, approximately 115 to 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente hace 115 y 110 millones de años, entre el Aptiense y Albiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Kryptops spans from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kryptops is based on partial skeletal remains found in Gadoufaoua in the western Ténéré Desert of Niger.
facts.quote: Se basa en un esqueleto parcial encontrado en Gadoufaoua en el desierto occidental de Teneré, Níger.

facts.statement: Only a single specimen of Kryptops is currently known to science.
facts.quote: Only one specimen of Kryptops is known.

facts.statement: Sereno and Brusatte conducted a cladistic analysis to demonstrate that Kryptops was the most basal member of the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Sereno y Brusatte realizaron un análisis cladístico para demostrar que Kryptops era el miembro más basal de la familia Abelisauridae.

facts.statement: Kryptops is placed within Abelisauridae as its oldest known member based on characteristics including a textured maxilla with vascular groove impressions and a narrow preorbital fossa.
facts.quote: Está basada en varias características, incluyendo un maxilar texturizado externamente por las impresiones de los surcos vasculares y una fosa anteorbital estrecha, que colocan claramente a Kryptops palaios dentro de Abelisauridae como su miembro más antiguo conocido.
